02-one-shot.py: 4 biology problems (2 errors, 1 warning, 1 note).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 0.909091 ul is below what the p20_single_gen2 can measure (1 ul at
least)
   line 79:  p20.aspirate(step, source)
   reached through: run:104 > transfer_volume:79
   At line 79 the p20_single_gen2 is asked to draw 0.909091 ul, below its minimum of 1 ul. A
   pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and
   the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells:
   well A1 in slot 4.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [96faddb659ad]

2. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 4: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 79:  p20.aspirate(step, source)
   reached through: run:104 > transfer_volume:79
   At line 79 the p20_single_gen2 draws 20 ul from water (well A1 in slot 4) with its tip 1
   mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 1,171 ul, which in this NEST 1
   Well Reservoir 195 mL reaches only 0.89 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air
   (this line did it 13 times, after 54 times in the liquid; 196 ul of air in all). The
   simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 5 wells filled from these
   draws got air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Also reached 5 other wells: wells B8, B9, B10, B11 and B12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 1,766 ul in it for the surface
   to reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a
   tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [a6098704a076]

3. WARNING UNMIXED-AT-END: 18 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4
and 14 more went in (5 to 23% of the well)
   line 80:  p20.dispense(step, dest)
   reached through: run:108 > transfer_volume:80
   At line 80 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 14 more to wells
   A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A8, A9 and 10 more in slot 3, which already held water (this line
   did it 18 times). The addition was 5 to 23% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a
   normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A8, A9 and 10 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A8, A9 and 10 more in slot 3 after line 80:
   `mix_after=(5, 20 to 40)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20 to 40, well)`, with the
   volume about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [03b57346b90d]

4. NOTE CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 20 stocks
   line 79:  p20.aspirate(step, source)
   reached through: run:108 > transfer_volume:79
   At line 79 the tip went into sample 1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2),
   sample 3 (well A3 in slot 2), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 16 more while it still
   carried water (well A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step (this line did it 20 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these
   stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from them
   again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for
   the next run.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 12 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 79 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [190bd36cf7df]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
